title: Command Palette: setting keyboard shortcut to anything reserved by the system causes issues
author: ilim-cell
summary: Command Palette lets users assign system-reserved chords such as Alt+Space even though the first press follows the Windows system-menu path, producing unreliable double-press activation.
next_action: Approve reserved-shortcut validation and activation handling.

confidence.rationale: The user-facing conflict is deterministic, but the preferred policy—support versus explicit rejection—requires maintainer confirmation.

judgment.rationale: CmdPal accepts a system-reserved activation chord such as Alt+Space, but the first press is consumed by the shell/window-menu path and only a rapid second press activates CmdPal. The editor should either register the chord reliably or reject it clearly.
evidence: The report gives a direct Alt+Space reproduction on PowerToys 0.100.0 and 0.100.2.
Another user confirms the double-press behavior.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve reserved-shortcut validation and activation handling.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt covers the scoped PowerToys-owned path identified by this lightweight judgment.

proposed_fixes.title: Validate or reliably register system-reserved CmdPal shortcuts
proposed_fixes.root_cause: CmdPal persists chords whose first key sequence is owned by Windows shell behavior without verifying that its activation registration can win consistently.
plan: Classify known shell-reserved chords during shortcut editing and test whether the activation mechanism can register them.
Reject unsupported chords with a specific conflict message, or route supported chords through one reliable low-level activation path.
Ensure a failed registration never leaves a saved shortcut that appears valid.
verification: Assign Alt+Space and verify it is either rejected with a clear reason or activates CmdPal on the first press.
Regression-test normal configurable shortcuts and window-menu behavior.

confidence.rationale: The user-facing conflict is deterministic, but the preferred policy—support versus explicit rejection—requires maintainer confirmation.

issue_context.summary: Command Palette lets users assign system-reserved chords such as Alt+Space even though the first press follows the Windows system-menu path, producing unreliable double-press activation.
known_information: Alt+Space is the concrete failing chord.
The shortcut editor accepts and saves it.
Two presses in quick succession activate CmdPal.
inferences: The configured chord is not being acquired with semantics strong enough to override the shell's reserved behavior.
Rejecting known-reserved chords may be safer than pretending they are reliable.
issue_context.analysis: The fix needs an explicit product decision implemented consistently: reserve/register the chord successfully, or block it with a specific conflict explanation.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full live body, attached diagnostic reference, comments, labels, and timeline.
Found no linked fix or ownership signal.

actions.label: Approve reserved-shortcut design
actions.design_summary: Reject unsupported reserved chords or register them reliably
actions.note: Approval starts a separate fork-side design workflow; this lightweight judgment contains no full design and performs no GitHub write.

actions.label: Reproduce Alt+Space double activation
actions.note: Maintainer-side verification only; this artifact does not execute the steps or write upstream.

reproduce.version_requirement: Latest stable or Preview PowerToys build
prerequisites: Set Command Palette activation to Alt+Space
steps: Press Alt+Space once and observe the result.
Repeat while different foreground windows are active.
reproduce.expected_result: The maintainer confirms whether the first press is consumed by Windows and can decide between reliable support and editor rejection.
